biography: David Makin, a name synonymous with inconsistency and occasional brilliance in the Australian racing scene, hails from a small sheep-farming town in New South Wales. His entry into motorsport was almost accidental. At 16, tinkering with his dad's old ute led to impromptu races across the dusty paddocks, honing a raw, untamed driving style. A local mechanic, spotting his talent, sponsored him in a state-level Formula Ford series. Makin showed flashes of speed, interspersed with spectacular crashes, earning him the moniker 'The Wrecking Ball'. He briefly flirted with Supercars but never quite found his footing, his inconsistent nature proving a liability. Currently, at 38, he’s a veteran presence in the lower tiers of the Aussie racing circuit with Team Racer Rubber, chasing the elusive consistency that has always dogged him.
drivingStyle: Makin's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He's known for late braking maneuvers and aggressive corner entries, often pushing his car to the absolute limit. While this can result in stunning overtakes and blistering lap times, it also leads to tire degradation and the occasional off-track excursion. He struggles to manage pressure situations, often cracking under duress and making unforced errors when leading.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision during the 2018 Bathurst 1000 support race. Rogers accused Makin of deliberately wrecking him.
A fierce on-track rivalry fueled by their contrasting driving styles. Sterling, known for her smooth and calculated approach, often clashes with Makin's aggressive tactics.
Peterson constantly criticizes Makin's inconsistent results, and refers to him as a lucky idiot.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of faded blue socks for every race.
Refuses to look at the weather forecast before a race, claiming it jinxes him.
Listens to a specific AC/DC song ('Highway to Hell') exactly three times before getting into the car.
famousQuote: "Sometimes you gotta send it, mate. Even if it means ending up in the sand trap."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2015 Queensland Raceway 300 after starting from the back of the grid due to a qualifying mishap. He carved his way through the field with a series of daring overtakes in the rain.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2019 Bathurst 6 Hour, gifting the victory to his arch-rival Ricky Rogers.
